name: Ideas That Taught the World to Think
description: From Socrates asking questions in Athens to the debates of the modern age: the great schools of philosophy in Greece, China, India and Europe, and the thinkers behind them.

checkpoints.name: The age of questions
checkpoints.note: In Greece, India and China, thinkers begin asking how we should live. Thales looks for natural causes, and Confucius, the Buddha, Laozi, Socrates, Plato and Aristotle each propose answers, their schools competing in the same few centuries.

checkpoints.name: Schools of the late ancient world
checkpoints.note: Stoics, Epicureans and sceptics teach ways to find calm in uncertain times, while Neoplatonists reach for the One. Augustine joins Christian faith to Greek thought, and Shankara in India argues that self and ultimate reality are the same.

checkpoints.name: Faith, reason and the new learning
checkpoints.note: Neo-Confucians in China, Scholastics in Europe, led by Thomas Aquinas, and humanists in Italy reread the classics. Then thinkers turn to experience and to reason alone as the sources of certain knowledge.

checkpoints.name: Modern debates
checkpoints.note: Kant and Hegel build vast systems, while Marx, utilitarians and Nietzsche test them. Philosophers weigh happiness, freedom and meaning, existentialists stress choice, and logical positivists try to clear away statements that cannot be tested.
